title: cross-lang: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics across python/ts/go, bump versions to v1.207.0
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: SDK surface area across Python/TypeScript/Go has drifted in how auth tokens, retry/backoff behavior, and streaming ergonomics are exposed. This causes integration bugs and makes cross-language parity harder to maintain. This PR unifies the behavior and developer ergonomics across the three SDKs and bumps the public package versions to v1.207.0. Changes include: consistent auth token refresh handling (single refresh-on-401 flow), retry policy parity (idempotency-aware defaults, jittered exponential backoff, configurable retry budget), and streaming API ergonomics (unified async/iterator shape, backpressure hints in TS and Go, simple blocking iterator for Python). Checklist: - [x] implement unified auth token provider interface in each SDK - [x] standardize default retry policy and expose config knobs - [x] harmonize streaming API signatures and examples - [x] update tests and integration harnesses - [x] bump package versions and changelogs - [x] run cross-lang integration tests and perf smoke-tests Compatibility & Migration notes: - Existing integrations that used SDK-specific retry config will continue to work but may observe slightly different default retry counts; customers can opt-in to legacy behavior via the legacy_retry_profile flag for one release. - Streaming shape change is additive in TS/Go (new helper wrappers provided). Python sees a minor ergonomic change (streaming generator now yields consistent event objects with explicit 'final' flag) - migration guide included. Testing performed: unit tests updated in all SDKs, e2e cross-language harness against local redwood test server, perf smoke runs on small/medium payloads. Rollout plan: staged publish for PyPI/NPM and Go modules with coordinated release notes and a short deprecation for legacy retry API. See linked Linear tickets for rollout gating.

feat(sdk-typescript): streaming iterator ergonomics + retry config parity
